title: Journey - Five Days of Gratitude - Day 3: Thanks in all things

parts.style: warm, gentle welcome, a soft smile in the voice, unhurried
parts.text: Welcome to Five Days of Gratitude. <short pause> This is day three, Thanks in All Things. <short pause> So far we have two sentences. You are good... and, This is from You. <short pause> Today's is the shortest, and it may be the hardest. <short pause> We'll take it slowly.

Find a position that's kind to your body. <short pause> If something hurts, you don't need to hide it for this. <short pause> Let your breath come as it comes. <short pause> And rest your two hands somewhere you can feel them... <short pause> on your knees, on a blanket, or simply at your sides.

There's a kind of gratitude that can be cruel. <short pause> It tells a person in pain to count their blessings. <short pause> It says, at least. <short pause> It says, others have it worse. <short pause> If anyone has ever handed you thankfulness like that, I'm sorry. <short pause> That is not what God is asking of you today.

Paul wrote to a young church in Thessalonica that was suffering for its faith. <short pause> They had real reasons to be afraid, and real losses to mourn. <short pause> He didn't tell them that those things were good. <short pause> What he wrote is in his first letter, chapter five, verse eighteen.

parts.style: reverent, very slow, reading scripture aloud
parts.text: In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: Listen to the first word. <short pause> In. <short pause> In the waiting room. <short pause> In the argument that isn't mended. <short pause> In the month with too little money. <short pause> You are not asked to give thanks for the illness, or the loss, or the harm that someone did to you. <short pause> Only that thanks may be allowed in the room with it.

parts.style: warm reassurance, slow, resting between sentences
parts.text: And giving thanks never means staying where you are being hurt. <short pause> If you are not safe, or it's all too heavy to carry, you can be grateful to God and still ask for help, right away. <short pause> Reaching for help can be part of His will for you, too.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Now, your hands. <short pause> Let one of them close gently, not tight, around the hard thing. <short pause> You don't have to solve it, or describe it nicely. <short pause> Just name it to God. <short pause> Lord, this is hard. <short pause> Let that hand stay closed for now. <short pause> He is not going to pry it open.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: And let the other hand turn over, and open. <short pause> It doesn't have to let go of anything, because it isn't holding the hard thing. <short pause> It is only free to receive. <short pause> Is there one thing that could rest there? <short pause> A person who checked on you. <short pause> An hour of sleep. <short pause> The strength that got you as far as this minute. <short pause> Or only this... that He has not left.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: Feel both hands at once. <short pause> One closed. One open. <short pause> Neither is lying. <short pause> The hard thing is true, and the gift is true, and both of these hands belong to you. <short pause> This is what thanks in all things can look like. <short pause> It doesn't take two open hands. <short pause> One is enough.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: So here is our third sentence, two words long. <short pause> Let's say it after the others. <short pause> You are good. <short pause> This is from You. <short pause> Even here. <short pause> If that's as much as you can say today, say only the last one. <short pause> Even here.

Let's pray. <short pause> Lord Jesus, You gave thanks and broke the bread on the night You were betrayed. <short pause> So You know how to hold sorrow and thanks together. <short pause> Take hold of the hand I cannot open. <short pause> Fill the one I can. <short pause> And where I have no thanks at all, stay with me until I do. <short pause> Amen.

parts.style: soft, warm, slow sending, resting between phrases
parts.text: When you meet the hard thing again today, you don't need a speech. <short pause> Just turn one hand over, wherever you are. <short pause> Under a table, in a pocket, on the wheel. <short pause> One open hand... <short pause> and two small words. <short pause> Even here.
